raw_case_text:
Mr. X, 80 years old farmer came to the consultation for the following signs: exertional dyspnea, chronic ulcerated and a burgeoning wound on the left foot, bleeding on contact for more than three months.
The disease started about three months prior to consultation and was marked by painful tumefaction, swelling and warmth of the sole of the foot, followed by desquamation and budding. The patient spent several weeks in the District Hospital of Batcham (West-Cameroon) and was put under cloxacillin at a dose of 2g per day for two months without success. The budding taking over the entire sole of the foot, the patient decided to consult the Center of Diagnostic and Treatment (CDT) of Tuberculosis of Baleng which, in addition to being the largest CDT in the West region of Cameroon, is also the center for detection and treatment of leprosy. Thus, the orientation of the patient in our hospital was motivated by a suspicion of leprosy. The family history of the patient was unremarkable.
The personal history of the patient showed that he was hypertensive with known heart failure for 05 years. He was under cardiurine (captopril 50mg / HCT 25mg) at a dose of one tablet daily and digoxin 0.25 mg at the dose of one tablet every 12 hours. Moreover he had a lipomectomy in 2009. Nothing else was remarkable. The physical examination of the patients revealed an impotence of the left lower limb and a painful wound on the sole of the foot on the same side. Overall, he is an octogenarian with an aspect of undernutrition and slight muscle lost. He presents a moderate hypertension (170/100 mm Hg) and a cardiac arrhythmia. The ulceration of the left foot was important and burgeoning, with few hemorrhagic foci and bleeding on contact. The diagnosis of malignancy with superinfection of the sole of the left foot in a hypertensive patient was made.
FBC: WBC: 5,5 x 103 /microl; RBC: 4,58 X 106 / microl; HGB:12.9 g/dL; MCV: 80 Fl MCH: 29 Pg; MCHC: 35.3g/dL; Plt: 275 x 103 /microl; fasting blood glucose: 0.89 G/L; urea: 0.42 G/L; creatinin: 6.10 mg/l; HIV serology was negative; test of leprosy on the lesion was negative.
Culture of the pus collected from the foot revealed the presence of Staphylococcus aureus (sensitive to cefixime, aminoside, amoxicillin and clavulanic acid, rifampicin). A biopsy was done on three different location of the wound. Microscopically, the sample showed a lesion that was focally ulcerated on the surface and superficial dermis. There was a lesion made of granulation tissue with elongated or oval vascular structures. These structures were made of non atypical benign endothelial with a mixed inflammatory infiltrate rich in fibroblasts. There was also a significant fibroblastique proliferation made up of elongated fusiform cells. On the surface, the flaps of malpighien epithelium were slightly hyperplastic: no malignancy. As a conclusion, it was a case of pyogenic granuloma also called botryomycome (Figure 1)
After the culture result indicating the presence of Staphylococcus aureus, and anatomopathologic analysis of biopsy suggestive of pyogenic granuloma, the patient's family refuse the surgical excision. The patient was then treated with ceftriaxone 1G X 2 per day and gentalline 80mg x 2 per day for 10 days, in addition to the daily treatment of wound after whashing with water containing betadine. The evolution of the patient was not very satisfactory, and surgical excision proposed again to the family, was again rejected. Moreover, taking in consideration the pharmacodynamics action of rifampicin and the effect of dapsone on the chronic leprous lesions, the following treatment was proposed to our patient: dapsone and rifampicin which were available free of cost in our Center. Our patient was then submitted to dapsone/rifampicin for a period of one month of treatment, the appointment was given at the end of the first wafer. After a month, the response was very encouraging with rather remarkable regression of the swelling and the total disappearance of exuding wounds which bled at the slightest touch.

subjective.chief_complaint: An 80-year-old male farmer from West Cameroon presented with exertional dyspnea and a 3-month history of a painful, burgeoning, contact-bleeding ulcerated mass over the sole of his left foot.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Three months prior to consultation, the patient developed painful swelling and warmth on the left sole that progressed to desquamation and an exophytic, bleeding ulcerated mass covering the plantar foot. Hospitalization at Batcham District Hospital and 2 months of oral cloxacillin (2 g/day) failed to halt progression, prompting referral to the Baleng Tuberculosis and Leprosy Diagnostic and Treatment Center for suspected leprosy.
subjective.past_medical_history: Five-year history of hypertension and heart failure treated with captopril 50 mg/hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg once daily and digoxin 0.25 mg every 12 hours; lipomectomy in 2009; unremarkable family history.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for exertional dyspnea, left foot pain, contact bleeding, and inability to bear weight on the left lower limb.

objective.physical_examination: The patient was an undernourished octogenarian with mild muscle wasting, moderate hypertension (170/100 mmHg), cardiac arrhythmia, functional impairment of the left lower limb, and a large, burgeoning, painful exophytic ulceration over the left sole with hemorrhagic foci and friable contact bleeding.
objective.routine_investigations: Full blood count showed WBC 5.5 x 10^3/uL, RBC 4.58 x 10^6/uL, hemoglobin 12.9 g/dL, MCV 80 fL, MCH 29 pg, MCHC 35.3 g/dL, and platelets 275 x 10^3/uL; fasting blood glucose was 0.89 g/L, urea 0.42 g/L, and creatinine 6.10 mg/L. HIV serology was negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Lesional leprosy testing was negative. Wound pus culture isolated Staphylococcus aureus susceptible to cefixime, aminoglycosides, amoxicillin-clavulanate, and rifampicin. Three-site plantar wound biopsies showed focal surface ulceration, hyperplastic malpighian epithelium without atypia, and granulation tissue containing elongated/oval benign vascular channels, a mixed fibroblast-rich inflammatory infiltrate, and fusiform fibroblastic proliferation without malignancy.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Histopathology and wound culture confirmed a giant plantar pyogenic granuloma (botryomycoma) superinfected with Staphylococcus aureus, ruling out squamous cell/melanocytic malignancy and leprosy. After the patient's family twice declined surgical excision and 10 days of parenteral ceftriaxone (1 g twice daily), gentamicin (80 mg twice daily), and daily povidone-iodine washes produced limited improvement, empirical combination therapy with oral dapsone and rifampicin for 1 month led to marked regression of the mass and complete resolution of exudation and contact bleeding.
